topic: How do atmospheric turbulence models like HVM affect optical link budget margin calculations for varying ground station altitudes?
consensus_response: Atmospheric turbulence models like HVM impact optical link budget margin calculations due to varying ground station altitudes. Increased altitude reduces atmospheric turbulence but decreases link distance, affecting free space loss and achievable data rates. A variable data rate concept is essential for high-altitude links, considering path-integrated aerosol content and link elevation effects on free space loss and achievable data rates. Temporal Coherence Time (TCT) influences the signal's ability to adapt to changing atmospheric conditions, impacting optimal symbol rate and coding scheme selection.
reference_context: Atmospheric turbulence affects optical links due to varying ground station altitudes, impacting signal attenuation, free space loss, and achievable data rates. Cloud coverage constitutes the predominant fading mechanism, resulting in link blockage. Fade mitigation techniques are considered to mitigate impairments caused by atmospheric turbulence, aerosols, and cirrus clouds.
